## Key terms

{{< glossary implication sufficient-condition necessary-condition contrapositive decision-table else-if-chain unreachable-rule state-machine edge-case test-case >}}

## 19.1 From words to conditions

- **and** → `&&` · **or** → `||` (also both) · **not, no** → `!`
- **either … or, not both** → `^` · **unless p** → if not p · **only if
  q** → … → q
- Give each fact a letter, then find the word that joins the two big parts.
- "Key and no skeleton, **or** thief" → `(k && !s) || t`.

![Rule words and their logic.](images/rule-words.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
`k && (!s || t)` looks similar, but then a thief needs a key.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Translate"}
Write as conditions: "The trap fires when the player steps on the plate and
is not flying"; "the red key or the blue key, but not both"; "the alarm
rings unless the guard is asleep".
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Words to logic"}
Choose the condition.

::: {.match extra="p -> !q|!(p || q)"}
plate pressed and not flying
:   p && !f

the red key or the blue key, but not both
:   r ^ b

the alarm rings unless the guard is asleep
:   alarm = !a

key and no skeleton, or thief
:   (k && !s) || t
:::
:::

## 19.2 If-then rules: sufficient and necessary

- In p → q: **p is sufficient** for q, **q is necessary** for p.
- **Contrapositive** ¬q → ¬p: the same rule. **Converse** q → p: not the
  same.
- "p **only if** q" = p → q.
- Only the case p = T, q = F breaks the rule.

![The implication, its contrapositive and its converse.](images/implication.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"If crown, then gate open" does **not** say "if gate open, then crown".
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · What follows?"}
Rule: "If the boss is defeated, the music changes." What follows when (a)
the boss is defeated; (b) the music did not change; (c) the music changed?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Crown and gate"}
Rule: crown → gate open. Choose what we know.

::: {.match extra="the gate will close|the player holds two crowns"}
The player holds the crown.
:   the gate is open

The gate is shut.
:   the player has no crown

The gate is open.
:   nothing about the crown

Which case breaks the rule?
:   crown, but the gate is shut
:::
:::

## 19.3 Decision tables

- One column per condition, **2^n rows**, and the **action** in each row.
- **Complete:** every row has an action. **No conflict:** never two actions.
- The guard: s = sees, n = near, w = weak; 8 rows; Flee in all rows with w.

![The decision table of the guard.](images/decision-table.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A table shows the cases that the designer forgot.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A trap table"}
The spike trap fires when the plate is pressed (p) and the trap is armed
(a), unless the player is flying (f). Make the 8-row table.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The guard table"}
Use the table of the guard. Choose the action.

::: {.match extra="Sleep|Jump"}
s = T, n = T, w = F
:   Attack

s = T, n = F, w = F
:   Chase

s = T, n = T, w = T
:   Flee

s = F, n = F, w = F
:   Patrol
:::
:::

## 19.4 Else-if chains: the order matters

- The chain is read from the top: **the first true rule wins**.
- A rule whose cases are all caught above it is **unreachable**.
- Most important and most specific rules first; `else` last.

![The same rules in a wrong and a right order.](images/rule-order.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/guard-brain.html" poster="sims/guard-brain.png" title="Guard Brain: rules, order and the decision table" height="900" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
`if (s)` before `else if (s && n)`: Attack never runs.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Order the rules"}
In **Guard Brain**, switch on s and n, then change the order until the
chain agrees with the designer in all 8 rows.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The chain"}
Use Guard Brain. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Patrol()|the last rule"}
In the first chain, which rule never runs?
:   Attack()

Which rule must come first?
:   Flee() if w

Which rule runs when two conditions are true?
:   the first true rule from the top

How many rows agree after the fix?
:   all 8
:::
:::

## 19.5 The guard as a state machine

- **States:** Patrol, Chase, Attack, Flee. **Transitions:** arrows with
  conditions.
- Each frame, check only the arrows that leave the current state.
- From every state, w leads to Flee.

![The guard as a state machine.](images/guard-states.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Two arrows from one state can be true together: give them an order.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Follow the guard"}
Start in Patrol. Frames: (1) s; (2) s, n; (3) s, ¬n; (4) ¬s; (5) w. Write
the state after each frame.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Next state"}
Choose the next state.

::: {.match extra="Sleep|Hide"}
In Patrol, the guard sees the player.
:   Chase

In Chase, the player comes near.
:   Attack

In Attack, the player walks away.
:   Chase

In Chase, the guard's health falls to 25.
:   Flee
:::
:::

## 19.6 Testing rules with edge cases

- A **test case** is one input with the expected result: one row of the
  table.
- An **edge case** tests the border of a number rule: for health < 30, test
  **29, 30, 31**.
- Bugs hide at `<` / `<=` and `>` / `>=`.

![Testing at the border of the rule.](images/edge-cases.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Tests with 10 and 80 never find the bug at 30.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Edge cases"}
"A bonus life when the player has at least 100 coins and less than 3
lives." Write four edge-case tests with the expected result.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Edge cases"}
Choose the test that finds the bug.

::: {.match extra="health = 50|speed = 100"}
Rule health < 30, code health <= 30.
:   health = 30

Rule speed > 5, code speed >= 5.
:   speed = 5

Rule coins >= 100, code coins > 100.
:   coins = 100

Rule lives < 3, code lives <= 3.
:   lives = 3
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Rule Smith {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The designer of *Torch Hall* gives six rules: the chest and the thief, the
bridge **unless** the lever is pulled, the boss room **only if** the
torches are lit, the crown and the shut gate, a guard chain with an
unreachable rule, and the flee rule with `<=`.

{{< sim file="sims/rule-smith.html" poster="sims/rule-smith.png" title="Rule Smith: exact rules, no bugs" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The rules of Torch Hall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="bridgeUp = l|nothing"}
The chest rule in code?
:   (k && !s) || t

The bridge stays up unless the lever is pulled.
:   bridgeUp = !l

A tester is in the boss room. What do we know?
:   the torches are lit

The gate is shut. What follows?
:   the player has no crown
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · Count the cases (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="6|12"}
How many rows has a table with 4 conditions?
:   16

In how many of 8 rows does (k ∧ ¬s) ∨ t open the chest?
:   5

In how many of 8 rows does the guard flee?
:   4

In how many of 8 rows does the guard attack?
:   1
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Give each fact a letter and translate and, or, not, unless, only if.
- p → q: p is sufficient, q is necessary; the contrapositive is the same
  rule, the converse is not.
- A decision table lists every case with one action.
- In an else-if chain the first true rule wins: special rules first.
- A state machine checks only the arrows that leave its state.
- Test every row, and test numbers at their borders.
